course.title: UAV Design: Foundations of Cyber-Physical Systems
course.subtitle: Master the foundations of UAV design, cyber-physical systems, and autonomous control
course.description:
Step into the world of intelligent aerial systems and discover how drones are transforming modern technology. This course takes you on a complete journey from the basic design and operation of UAVs to the advanced computing and networking methods that make them smart, connected, and autonomous. We begin with the foundations: frames, motors, sensors, flight controllers, and the logic of modular, open platforms that make upgrades and experimentation easy. From there, you'll learn how drones communicate over air-to-air and air-to-ground links, compare Wi-Fi and cellular (4G/5G) paths, and see when to use directional antennas, relays, or mesh networking for reliable coverage.

You'll then explore how drones collect, process, and share data using onboard computing, edge AI, and high-speed communication. Through clear explanations and real examples, you'll see how distributed computing, coordinated control, and 5G connectivity enable missions like search-and-rescue, inspection, mapping, and multi-UAV cooperation. We'll also connect communication and control through co-design principles: reinforcement-learning-based antenna alignment, swarm coordination, mobility models for safe airspace sharing, and practical strategies to reduce latency and energy use while maintaining link quality.

The final module focuses on airborne computing and AI: selecting Jetson/Intel boards, using containers and virtualization (Docker/KVM), and scaling intelligence across fleets with federated and coded computing. Each module builds on the last starting with drone architecture, moving through communication systems and control, and culminating in advanced edge computing and AI for resilient swarms. Whether you're an engineering student, researcher, or drone enthusiast, this course equips you with the knowledge to understand, evaluate, and build next-generation UAV technologies that compute, communicate, and collaborate in the real world.
course.welcomeMessage:
Hello and welcome to UAV Computing and Networking: From Basic to Advanced!

I'm excited to have you here. In this course, we'll explore how drones are evolving into intelligent systems that can compute, communicate, and collaborate. Take your time, follow each module in order, and make notes as you go — it will help connect all the concepts easily.

If you have any questions or feedback during the course, feel free to share them. Let's begin your journey into the world of next-generation UAVs!
course.congratulationsMessage:
Congratulations on completing UAV Computing and Networking: From Basic to Advanced!

You've gained a strong foundation in UAV hardware, communication, control, and airborne computing. I hope you're inspired to keep exploring advanced drone technologies and real-world applications.

Don't forget to leave a review and share your learning experience — your feedback helps improve the course for future learners.

Best wishes as you continue building and innovating in the world of UAVs!
learningOutcomes: Fundamentals of UAV systems: quadrotors vs. fixed-wing UAVs, flight controllers, sensors, and onboard computing
The concept of an Open Airborne Computing Platform modular design for research and prototyping
Basics of UAV communication: air-to-air and air-to-ground links, Wi-Fi vs. cellular networks, directional antennas
Networking opportunities and challenges: latency, bandwidth limits, energy constraints, safety, and regulations
Virtualization & Containers (Docker, KVM) for UAV computing flexibility and security
Control and Co-Design: how communication and control must work together, including reinforcement learning solutions
Distributed UAV computing: swarm intelligence, coded computing, and federated learning
Real-world applications: disaster recovery, emergency communications, agriculture, inspection, drone swarms, and smart cities
prerequisites: Basic understanding of computer networks and programming (Python/C++ helpful but not mandatory)
Familiarity with electronics or embedded systems is useful but not required
No prior experience with drones is needed — the course will guide you from fundamentals to advanced topics
targetAudience: Students in Electrical, Electronics, Computer, or Aerospace Engineering curious about UAVs
Researchers exploring drone technology and autonomous systems
Hobbyists and drone enthusiasts wanting to understand the technical side
Anyone excited about the future of drones, flying taxis, and smart city integration

instructor.name: Dr. Yan Wan, Dr. Junfei Xie, Dr. Kejie Lu, Dr. Shengli Fu
instructor.title: Professors of Cyber-Physical Systems
instructor.bio: With over 15 years of experience in UAV research and development, I've worked on cutting-edge projects in drone communication, swarm intelligence, and airborne computing. My passion is making complex UAV technology accessible to everyone.

modules.title: Module 1: Open Airborne Computing Platforms
modules.description: Learn how modern drones are designed as modular systems that combine control, communication, and onboard computing. This lecture covers UAV hardware basics — from frames and motors to controllers and sensors — and explains how open airborne platforms make it easier to test, upgrade, and integrate new technologies for real-world applications.

modules.title: Quiz 1: Open Airborne Computing Platforms
modules.description: Test your understanding of UAV hardware, regulations, and Single Board Computers.

questions.question: The maximum flight height for a drone is:
questions.explanation: Under FAA regulations, the maximum altitude for recreational and commercial drone operations is 400 feet above ground level.

questions.question: The open aerial computing platform is to:
options: Design a drone specifically for taking selfies
questions.explanation: The open aerial computing platform aims to create affordable, modular drone systems that can be easily customized and upgraded.

questions.question: The safety for drone operation includes:
questions.explanation: Comprehensive drone safety encompasses the physical safety of the drone itself, the operator, and the airspace/environment where it operates.

questions.question: Under current FAA regulations, can we fly a drone beyond visual line of sight?
questions.explanation: Current FAA regulations generally require drones to remain within visual line of sight (VLOS) unless special waivers are obtained.

questions.question: Which is NOT another name for drones?
questions.explanation: While quadrotors, UAVs, and eVTOLs are all types of unmanned aerial vehicles, a traditional helicopter is a manned aircraft.

questions.question: What is a Single Board Computer (SBC)?
options: A processor chip used in PCs
A complete computer on one circuit board
questions.explanation: An SBC integrates all computer components (CPU, memory, I/O) onto a single circuit board, making it compact and suitable for embedded applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an SBC?
questions.explanation: Raspberry Pi 4 is a popular single board computer that includes CPU, RAM, and I/O ports on one board.

questions.question: What distinguishes an SBC from a traditional PC?
options: SBCs cannot run any operating system
SBCs are larger and more expensive
SBCs integrate CPU, memory, and I/O on a single board
questions.explanation: SBCs are distinguished by their integration of all essential computer components on a single compact board.

questions.question: Which OS is commonly used with SBCs like Raspberry Pi?
questions.explanation: Raspberry Pi OS, based on Linux, is specifically optimized for Raspberry Pi single board computers.

questions.question: What is the typical application of an SBC?
options: Running compact home servers or robotics projects
questions.explanation: SBCs are ideal for compact applications like home servers, IoT devices, and robotics due to their small size and low power consumption.

modules.title: Module 2: UAV Communications and Networking
modules.description: Discover how UAVs communicate and form flying networks. You'll explore air-to-air and air-to-ground links, the use of Wi-Fi, cellular, and 5G/6G systems, and how drones can serve as relays, base stations, or connected nodes. This session also introduces networking challenges and modern solutions like SDN, NFV, and multi-access edge computing.

modules.title: Quiz 2: UAV Communications and Networking
modules.description: Assess your knowledge of UAV communication modes, applications, and design guidelines.

questions.question:
According to the video, which of the following modes belong to UAV communications?

A. Air-to-air

B. Air-to-ground

C. Air-to-satellite

D. Ground-to-satellite
questions.explanation: UAV communications include air-to-air (between drones), air-to-ground (drone to ground station), and air-to-satellite modes. Correct answer: A, B, C.

questions.question: According to the video, what is the main role of UAV in 3GPP release 17?
questions.explanation: In 3GPP Release 17, UAVs are primarily considered as user equipment (UE) in cellular networks.

questions.question:
According to the video, which of the following are possible applications of airborne computing for communications and networking?

A. Controlling the trajectory of a UAV-enabled base station

B. Recording videos on a UAV

C. Sending videos from a UAV to a control center

D. Identifying a vehicle on a UAV and then using directional antenna to communicate with the vehicle
questions.explanation: Airborne computing enables trajectory control for UAV base stations and intelligent directional antenna alignment. Correct answer: A, D.

questions.question:
According to the video, what are the main challenges in the design and deployment of airborne computing for communications and networking?

A. Diverse application requirements

B. Limitations of UAV platform

C. Regulation of frequency allocation

D. Patent of technology
questions.explanation: The main challenges include diverse application requirements and UAV platform limitations. Correct answer: A, B.

questions.question:
According to the video, what are design guidelines for using airborne computing to enhance communications and networking?

A. Identifying the computing needs

B. Clarifying the system model

C. Specifying the computing model

D. Understanding the relevant factors
options: A, B, C, D (All of the above)
questions.explanation: All listed items are important design guidelines: identifying computing needs, clarifying the system model, specifying the computing model, understanding relevant factors, and optimizing system performance. Correct answer: A, B, C, D.

questions.question:
According to the video, what are the desired features of enabling technologies for using airborne computing to enhance communications and networking?

A. Improving the capabilities of UAV

B. Improving the scalability

C. Providing flexibility

D. Reducing the cost of UAV
questions.explanation: Desired features include improving UAV capabilities, scalability, and flexibility. Correct answer: A, B, C.

modules.title: Module 3: Networked Control and Co-Design
modules.description: This section brings communication and control together. You'll see how drones keep their antennas aligned using reinforcement learning, how they share information while moving, and how swarm coordination works when many UAVs fly together. We'll introduce models that explain how drones move randomly in real airspaces, and how safe integration is managed when multiple UAVs share the sky. You'll also learn about game theory and distributed control tools that help drones cooperate without collisions. By the end, you'll know how control and communication must be co-designed to make UAV systems safe, reliable, and scalable.

modules.title: Quiz 3: Networked Control and Co-Design
modules.description: Evaluate your understanding of networked UAV systems, directional antennas, and co-design principles.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of a networked UAV system?
options: To enable multiple UAVs to communicate, coordinate, and perform complex missions
questions.explanation: Networked UAV systems enable multiple drones to work together through communication and coordination to accomplish complex missions.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using directional antennas on UAVs?
options: They provide long-range, high-bandwidth communication without ground infrastructure
questions.explanation: Directional antennas focus signal energy in specific directions, enabling long-range, high-bandwidth communication.

questions.question: When GPS signals are unavailable, which signal can be used to aid antenna alignment?
questions.explanation: RSSI provides signal strength information that can be used to optimize antenna alignment when GPS is unavailable.

questions.question: In a co-design framework, what best describes the relationship between communication and control?
options: Communication supports control, but not vice versa
Control helps communication, and communication helps control
questions.explanation: In co-design, communication and control are interdependent - each supports and enhances the other.

questions.question: Which learning method can adaptively estimate parameters in a UAV communication model?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning can adaptively learn and estimate communication parameters through interaction with the environment.

questions.question: What happens when both GPS and RSSI are combined for antenna alignment?
options: No change in performance is observed
questions.explanation: Combining GPS position data with RSSI signal strength information provides more robust and accurate antenna alignment.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of random mobility models in UAV network design?
options: To represent unpredictable UAV movement for analysis
questions.explanation: Random mobility models help analyze and design UAV networks by representing realistic, unpredictable movement patterns.

questions.question: Which factor increases the safety of UAV airspace?
options: Longer flight times and smoother movement patterns
questions.explanation: Longer flight times and smoother, more predictable movement patterns enhance safety by reducing collision risks.

modules.title: Module 4: UAV AI Applications
modules.description: Explore how drones act as flying computers. This lecture focuses on onboard AI processing, comparison of computing boards like Jetson and Intel, and virtualization tools such as Docker and KVM. You'll also learn how UAVs share workloads through distributed and federated computing, enabling smarter, faster, and more resilient swarm operations.

modules.title: Quiz 4: UAV AI Applications
modules.description: Test your knowledge of onboard computing, virtualization, and distributed computing for UAVs.

questions.question: Why is doing computation onboard a UAV often better than offloading to the ground?
options: Avoids bandwidth limits and transmission delays
questions.explanation: Onboard computation avoids bandwidth limitations and transmission delays, enabling real-time processing for time-critical tasks.

questions.question: In the three-layer architecture, what does the virtualization infrastructure layer do?
options: Virtualizes hardware so resources can be allocated flexibly
questions.explanation: The virtualization layer abstracts physical hardware resources, allowing flexible allocation to different applications.

questions.question: Which was not a key criterion for choosing a UAV single-board computer?
questions.explanation: Low weight is desired for UAVs; high mass would reduce flight time and maneuverability.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about KVM vs Docker?
options: KVM provides stronger isolation and security than Docker and requires fewer system resources
They perform identically in terms of overhead and isolation
Docker provides stronger isolation and security than KVM
Docker containers are lighter and faster to start than KVM virtual machines but have weaker isolation
questions.explanation: Docker containers are more lightweight but provide weaker isolation compared to KVM virtual machines.

questions.question: What's the main security/performance trade-off mentioned?
options: VMs = stronger isolation but higher overhead
Containers = most secure and most resource-hungry
questions.explanation: Virtual machines provide stronger security isolation but consume more system resources than containers.

questions.question: Which is a listed benefit of virtualization for UAVs?
options: Run multiple apps concurrently on one UAV
questions.explanation: Virtualization enables running multiple applications simultaneously with resource isolation and management.

questions.question: In coded distributed computing with two workers on A1 and A2, adding a third worker computing (A1 + A2)X lets the master:
options: Finish only after all three respond
Finish after any two results arrive
questions.explanation: Coded computing adds redundancy, allowing the master to complete computation once any two workers respond.

questions.question: What's the key idea of BPCC?
options: Let workers send partial batch results early for approximate solutions
questions.explanation: Batched and Packed Coded Computing (BPCC) allows workers to send partial results early, reducing overall completion time.

questions.question: In BPCC encoding, the matrix H should be chosen so that:
options: It depends only on input size
questions.explanation: The encoding matrix H must have any R rows be full-rank to enable reconstruction from any R worker responses.

questions.question: For dynamic BPCC with a master and N workers doing matrix–vector tasks, how many worker failures can be tolerated?
questions.explanation: Dynamic BPCC can tolerate up to N-1 worker failures, completing as long as at least one worker (or the master) functions.
